title: Semantic grid tables lose the deck source and evade missing-source findings
description:
## Description
DeckSpec kind:table loses meta.source after compilation to a one-cell shape_grid. All ten production templates, including p-style, omit visible attribution on quantitative slide 5, and no missing-source finding is emitted. Neighboring charts inherit the same source.

## Steps to Reproduce
Render .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/quantitative/deckspec-v2-p-style.json, inspect physical slide 5. Repeat across the ten coverage.json templates. Adding slides[4].source (deckspec-v3-p-style.json) restores the attribution, confirmed in OOXML and table-source-control-p-style.png. Durable inputs/evidence: tests/quality/results/consulting-benchmark-20261003/.

## Actual Behavior
internal/semantic/slides/table.go CompileTable uses blankTitleCellSlide (ngbnf). cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_source.go slideDataKind checks Content and pattern/compose allowlists but never grid cells. internal/semantic/compile.go supplies the default only for KindRegions, not KindTable. Both inheritance and missing-source detection therefore miss the table. This is distinct from go-slide-creator-1jtn7: that issue concerns quantitative content in the deliberately excluded table-highlight pattern.

## Expected Behavior
Quantitative semantic tables inherit deck-level source; missing attribution is diagnosed when neither source exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Verify visible meta.source on numeric tables across all ten production templates, including p-style.
- Explicit slide source overrides the default without duplicates; source bands preserve readable table geometry.
- Include currency, percentage and period values, missing source, qualitative-only table controls, and raw grid table classification as appropriate.
- Validate and render agree; inspect actual PNGs as well as XML.

title: Horizontal negative-bar values occupy the category-label column
description:
## Description
Engine geometry: three short category names, three values [3, 2.5, -0.5], and one series. No unusual density. Changing orientation is an author workaround, not a horizontal-renderer correction.
Both p-style and modern-yellow controls generate with deterministic_ready=true despite a visible North / -0.5 collision. The info-level text_overlap finding does not prevent readiness.

## Steps to Reproduce
Use .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/quantitative/negative-control-p-style.json, .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/quantitative/negative-control-modern-yellow.json with render_deck_spec, then render_deck_thumbnails at 100 DPI. Evidence and portable inputs will be in tests/quality/results/consulting-benchmark-20261003/.

## Actual Behavior
horizontalLayout adds valueReserve to plot.X for negative bars, but drawHorizontalCategoryNames anchors the category relative to that new plot.X. The most-negative bar ends at plot.X; its right-aligned value then occupies the same left band as the right-aligned category. The reserve moves both labels together rather than separating them.

Reserve separate category and negative-value columns. Preserve values, zero line and readability. This is distinct from closed go-slide-creator-5na8e (vertical lower edge).

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Image-case screenshots are cover-cropped with no contain option
description:
Consulting benchmark round, HEAD85b482d3; parent go-slide-creator-kes55.

WHAT / OUTPUT IMPACT
The default semantic image_case supports a screenshot as evidence but its image-text-split composition always cover-crops it, with no exposed contain control. A1600x1000 synthetic operating dashboard loses its full corporate header and the bottom next-action row in the p-style slide. The caption describes evidence, yet some supplied evidence is silently off-slide. Parent visually compared source PNG and final100DPI slide; this is actual crop, not text extraction.

## Steps to Reproduce
Strategy fixture: .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/strategy/p-style-spec-r3/spec.json, slide9 kind:image_case, image.path approval-workbench.png. Rendered evidence: p-style-spec-r3/slide-09.png; full source: strategy/approval-workbench.png. Source top reads HELIOS / CASH OPERATIONS; source bottom says Next action: assign all unowned cases by16:00. Both disappear from the rendered image. The body and source line otherwise remain intact. Agent also observed cropping in abstract/modern attempts; p-style is independently confirmed.

CAUSE
internal/patterns/pattern_photo.go:PhotoSchema exposes only path,url,alt. internal/patterns/image_text_split.go:itsImageColumn builds a new GridImageInput from those three fields and a GridCellInput with no Fit, so the image uses cover. The shared native picture-placeholder contain support does not reach this semantic pattern.

EXPECTED / SCOPE
Allow evidence screenshots and complete exhibits to request contain (and preserve that choice through DeckSpec, shared photo schema, expansion and grid rendering). Keep cover available for photographic cases. A screenshot must preserve header, footer and evidence bounds unless the author deliberately requests a crop. If the complete image is too small to read, report that and offer an evidence-region/detail layout; do not silently crop it to make the frame look full.

## Acceptance Criteria
Render the same image_case with explicit contain and cover under p-style and narrow/wide tracked templates. Confirm source-edge markers and next-action row remain visible for contain; cover remains intentionally cropped; verify alt text and source line survive. Test the schema and compiled Fit passthrough as well as actual rendered images.

DEDUP
Closed3qzo4.14/3qzo4.15 concern native picture-placeholder contain/readability. Closedkkc5t concerns source-coordinate annotations under crop. This is the separate image_case/image-text-split authoring contract that cannot express whole-exhibit preservation.
notes: Final individual-image review correction: material screenshot content is lost on six templates (p-style, business-template, blue-corporate, modern-yellow, abstract, modern-template). Midnight-blue, forest-green and warm-coral retain the full banner, four rows and action line despite nonzero geometric cropping and are visually approved for this case. Do not equate nonzero crop with content loss.

title: Line-chart endpoint labels reuse low-contrast series colors in p-style
description:
Consulting benchmark round, HEAD85b482d3; parent go-slide-creator-kes55.

WHAT
Direct series labels inherit low-contrast template chart colors without readable text treatment. In the p-style presentation-scale control, the essential 'Current capacity' endpoint label is #d89060 on white (2.600:1); 'Demand' is #fd5108 (3.303:1). These labels are visibly faint compared with the black chart labels. The capacity label falls below even the3:1 large-text threshold. No contrast diagnostic is emitted. The midnight-blue control using the same data is readable, making this a real template-dependent output gap rather than changed input.

## Steps to Reproduce
.claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/portability/present-control-p-style/spec.json, deck.pptx, slide-2.png (100DPI, visually inspected), chart.svg extracted from ppt/media/image1.svg.
meta.viewing_mode=present, meta.type_scale=presentation; slide2 kind chart_insight, line_chart, two series Demand [80,90,100,120] and Current capacity [100,100,100,100]. Endpoint labels are font-weight500, font-size19.1887 SVG units; background white. Exact sRGB relative luminance calculation yields ratios above. The screenshot retains all series data; this issue concerns labeling contrast, not forecast semantics or an axis-baseline rule.

CAUSE
svggen/charts.go LineChart.drawLegendOrDirectLabels -> seriesLabelColors -> drawLineDirectSeriesLabels. svggen/series_highlight.go seriesLabelColors returns the palette colors unchanged when no highlight is set, and only replaces non-highlighted colors otherwise. Endpoint text therefore reuses a color suitable for a brand series stroke even when it is unsuitable for legible text. The OOXML text contrast pass cannot repair SVG text inside the chart.

EXPECTED
Keep series identity and template branding while giving endpoint text a readable color for its actual background and effective size (for example a suitable template ink plus a colored connector/key). Enforce or report low contrast in chart text, including direct labels with and without a highlighted series. Do not solve this by replacing all brand-colored series graphics with black.

## Acceptance Criteria
Render this two-series control under p-style and representative light/warm/dark tracked templates. Check emitted SVG foreground/background contrast and inspect final PPTX raster images; ensure each label still maps unambiguously to its series. Cover explicit series colors and highlighted/non-highlighted paths.

DEDUP
Searched all-status contrast and line issues. Closed OOXML shape/template contrast fixes do not cover SVG endpoint labels; prior direct-label overlap issues and series highlighting address different behavior.

title: Quantitative option matrices omit the deck source and evade missing-source review
description:
Consulting benchmark round, HEAD 85b482d3; parent go-slide-creator-kes55.

WHAT / OUTPUT IMPACT
An option_matrix using scale:text to compare monetary spend and capacity figures silently omits the deck-level meta.source. The rendered matrix shows $0 / $0.4m / $1.2m and 0k / 25k orders with no attribution or illustrative-data disclosure. Generation returns deterministic_ready:true, input score100, and no DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE warning. This reproduces across all four portability fixtures. Explicit per-slide source is a workaround.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run the current binary:
json2pptx semantic render --spec .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/portability/portability-side-logo/spec.json --templates-dir tests/quality/fixtures/portability/templates --output /tmp/matrix-source.pptx
Inspect slide5 vs slide3. meta.source is 'Illustrative planning case; figures are synthetic'; slide3 renders it; slide5 does not. Slide5 is kind:option_matrix, scale:text, three options with quantitative money/capacity scores. Rendered evidence: portability-side-logo/slide-5.png (100DPI) and deck.pptx. Same slide5 in portability-4x3, portability-21x9, portability-two-master.

CAUSE
cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_source.go:dataSourcePatterns excludes table-highlight because qualitative Harvey/RAG judgments do not need a default source. slideDataKind and applyDeckSourceDefault classify by pattern name rather than examining a text-scale matrix's numeric content. Both inheritance and missing-source findings skip legitimate quantitative comparison tables.

EXPECTED / SCOPE
Recognize numerical text-scale option matrices as data-bearing, apply meta.source once unless overridden, and emit DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE when neither default nor explicit source exists. Preserve the deliberate exemption for wholly qualitative Harvey/RAG judgments; do not indiscriminately add footnotes to all pattern slides. Preserve explicit source precedence and the single source zone.

## Acceptance Criteria
Cover quantitative text-scale matrix with default source, explicit override, and neither; qualitative Harvey/RAG controls should retain existing behavior. Render the quantitative matrix in p-style, a tracked production template, and a portability fixture; verify the visible source appears once and does not overlap the takeaway. Include a semantic path in the missing-source finding.

DEDUP
Related closed cuszt (source zone), mp2p4 (default source), zmjs (explicit sources on all kinds), fn2ka (regions inheritance). This is the remaining quantitative option-matrix classification hole, not a request to repeat those implementations.
notes: Additional current-head controls reproduce the missing visible source in p-style and midnight-blue: .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/portability/source-control-{p-style,midnight-blue}/spec.json, deck.pptx, slide-1.png. Both generated successfully and both PNGs inspected at100DPI. Explicit source workaround verified visually across21x9, side-logo andtwo-master final decks.

title: Generic autofit diagnostics misclassify KPI captions as body text
description:
## Description
A valid 10.08pt KPI caption blocks deterministic readiness because the generic OOXML autofit scan labels the entire mixed stat box as body text. Role-aware validation accepts the same revision. This is a diagnostic consistency defect, not a demonstrated visual readability failure.

## Steps to Reproduce
Render quantitative/deckspec-v4-modern.json under .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/. In render-v4-modern.json result.structuredContent.diagnostics[1], slide_index 7, raw_path /slides/7/rendered_shapes/206 emits TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN warning: body text renders at 10.1pt below 12pt. Generation succeeds but deterministic_ready=false and slide 8 scores 80. suspect-geometry.json shows shape 206 containing 17% and FY26 EBIT margin, caption 14pt times stored autofit 72% = 10.08pt. Durable inputs/evidence: tests/quality/results/consulting-benchmark-20261003/.

## Actual Behavior
internal/generator/autofit_readability.go:104 unconditionally uses TextRoleBody in the generic XML scan. Role-aware grid validation uses caption semantics. internal/tokens/typography.go:18 explicitly classifies KPI labels as captions, with a 10pt presentation floor. The final revision has no role-aware validation readability violation.

## Expected Behavior
Generic generated-text diagnostics preserve or recover paragraph roles and agree with the documented role floors. Do not report a compliant caption as failing body text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The reproduced 10.08pt KPI caption does not emit a false body-floor finding or prevent deterministic readiness.
- Captions genuinely below 10pt and body paragraphs below 12pt still trigger their correct findings in present mode.
- Test mixed KPI figure/caption boxes with stored autofit, and preserve stricter presentation-scale requirements where applicable.
- Validate and render agree on role and threshold; inspect slide 8 without enlarging the caption merely to evade a wrong role.

title: Account for usable plot height in stacked chart and supporting-table regions
description:
## Description
Support a usable stacked-chart plus supporting-table composition. A reference-inspired, modest three-period/four-series exhibit allocates only 16-36 SVG units of vertical plot height after axis, heading and legend space, causing Y tick overlap. This is a capability/allocation improvement, not an undetected defect: deterministic_ready=false and diagram.text_overlap are correctly emitted.

Original 70/30 chart/table allocation truthfully refuses table rows; bounded repair to 60/40 preserves the table but collapses the chart. Q1/Q2/Q3 and four short series avoid the earlier rotated-label issue. Durable inputs/evidence: tests/quality/results/consulting-benchmark-20261003/.

## Actual Behavior
p-style plot span 36.1323 and tick spacing 12.0189 versus 19.1936px labels; midnight-blue span 28.1197, spacing 9.3732; modern-template span 16.1386, spacing 5.3669. Percentage allocation in regions.go precedes fixed decoration requirements in cartesian_layout.go. Requesting two Y ticks still produces four nice ticks 0/20/40/60. Closed k478 addressed rotated long labels; 0ncd8 dry-render geometry and 72qai finding emission work here.

## Expected Behavior
Provide usable plot/table allocation or an actionable alternative before producing a cramped exhibit. A larger chart, side-by-side arrangement or split slide is a valid author fallback.

- Preserve all three periods, four series, totals and two supporting rows, with clear labels on all three tested templates.
- If no stacked layout fits, offer an actionable alternative rather than repeated text shortening; retain the current overlap gate.

title: Shared-cell fit repairs attach whole-cell budgets to a single eyebrow or label
description:
Consulting benchmark round at HEAD85b482d3. Parent go-slide-creator-kes55.

WHAT / OBSERVED
- Modern strip label Capture (7chars) remains9.84pt after long labels become one word; all4label findings ask shorten_text. The original label max_chars budget is larger than current label, so the advertised limit gives no usable reduction.
- Midnight image_case eyebrow PILOT DESIGN (12chars, under documented30) maps to a12pt paragraph rendering10.8pt. Primary apply_patch asks to rewrite that eyebrow to at most532characters, strategy split. That budget is the shared cell budget rather than an eyebrow-specific safe limit.
- Removing the optional eyebrow and retaining narrative/bullets/metrics gets past this refusal; increasing or rewriting the eyebrow alone is not a sensible repair.
- These are guidance defects independent of whether the source can fit: a valid refusal may remain, but its primary suggested edit must address the constrained region.

CAUSE
worstReadability identifies the worst paragraph and attaches paragraph_text. retargetCellReadabilityFix then adds maxChars for the entire grid cell. Semantic mapping identifies the individual authored field using paragraph_text, while retaining the cell-wide max_chars. Thus the patch edits only an eyebrow/label with a budget measured for the shared cell. Joint height constraints are hidden from that edit.
